hook_text: You've already lived through a business cycle. You just didn't know its name.
clip_script: Call up a year you remember when things flowed: the rank humming, shops putting up help-wanted signs, everyone's cousin suddenly employed. Now a year when everything pinched: quiet tills, shortened shifts, come back next year, maybe. Same town, same people — different YEARS. That difference, repeating down the decades, is the business cycle: the economy breathing in and breathing out. Breathing in — the upswing: more customers means more hiring means more customers. Full lungs — the peak: everything at full stretch, prices creeping. Breathing out — the downswing: orders thin, cuts spread, bad news forwarding itself down the street. Empty — the trough: the hardest months, yet prices are low, loans are cheaper, worn-out things need replacing — and one morning, the orders start again. The breath never runs on a timetable. But two quarters in a row of shrinking production has a name: recession. Now you can read the news like an economist.
visual_style: A township main street that brightens and dims like slow breathing — signs flipping from HIRING to CLOSED and back, overlaid with a glowing wave curve that labels itself upswing, peak, downswing, trough as the street changes.
pacing: Slow inhale-exhale rhythm matching the street's brightening and dimming, with a crisp spoken-definition beat on 'recession' before the final line.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and learn to read the economy's breathing.
